epics.title: Retire oversized provider sessions across runner restarts
epics.objective: Bound turn cost and checkpoint growth by retiring a persistent provider session on its next resume once its observed context crosses a global cap, and reclaim DeepAgents checkpoint state through a provider-neutral release port.

tasks.title: Measurement, storage, and the quality gate
tasks.objective: Give every persistent provider session a typed context high-water mark and the fenced repository operations that raise and retire it, teach both adapters to report model-visible input (including on error frames) with explicit per-route cache semantics, make resetScope return the references it removes, and put the diff-scoped npm run lint:changed under verify and CI as the blocking gate, with full npm run lint advisory. After this task the host can measure and retire, but no policy fires yet.
acceptance_criteria: S1 derivation: modelVisibleInputTokens returns 271,500 for an Anthropic usage of 1,000 input / 270,000 cache read / 500 cache write; 1,000 for an OpenAI-compatible usage of 1,000 input / 800 cached; the additive form for a mixed or unresolved route; totalBillableInputTokens and all other billing fields unchanged; the route resolves from usage.modelRoute and falls back to usage.provider when modelRoute is absent (provider fallback).

S2/R2 partial usage, spawned runners: an errored Claude worker run and an errored DeepAgents worker run each write one cumulative partial-usage payload with the turn's usageEventId on their single error frame; Claude carries it as a typed QueryFailure thrown from the result branch and written by runner/index.ts; DeepAgents carries it as a typed DeepAgentPartialUsage value passed stream-normalizer → deep-agent-runner → index. A close-driven abort keeps its own identity: the partial usage rides on the abort instead of replacing it, so a graceful stop is never turned into an error frame, proven at the unit seam and by the Node-24 runner boundary _close test.

S2/R2 partial usage, inline lanes: an errored Claude inline-lane turn and an errored DeepAgents inline-lane turn each emit one terminal error output carrying the accumulated usage with the turn's usageEventId.

S3 storage: provider_sessions.context_high_water_mark is a nullable integer column added by a generated drizzle migration (db:migrations:check clean); raiseProviderSessionContextHighWaterMark keeps the larger value, leaves metadata_json untouched, rejects a stale owner, ignores non-resumable rows, rejects non-integer or negative values before SQL with ProviderSessionMeasurementError, and returns whether a row changed; the turn-context projection returns contextHighWaterMark.

R1 fences: raise and retireProviderSession compare agent_sessions.reset_at with IS NOT DISTINCT FROM the caller's generation; a null/null generation succeeds and null versus non-null is rejected on both operations.

R1 retirement: retireProviderSession is one atomic active→expired UPDATE fenced on id, agent_session_id, provider, external_session_id, status='active' and the generation, returning { providerSessionId, externalSessionId, executionProviderId } or undefined; the fingerprint-change, missing-session and ops-service facade callers switch to it, while the compaction-delta degradation path keeps the existing expireProviderSession helper unchanged (0159 §4).

R3 registry: every executable route's cacheSupport.prompt declares cacheReadsIncludedInInput and cacheWritesIncludedInInput (type in model-provider-registry.ts); the registry validator fails a route missing either; nonzero OpenAI and OpenRouter cache-write usage yields inputTokens unchanged; DeepAgents normalised usage carries the resolved provider and modelRoute.

R4 return type: resetScope returns an immutable list of retired { providerSessionId, externalSessionId, executionProviderId } selected FOR UPDATE before delete and returned after commit, and a readonly empty list on no-route or empty paths; canonical-session-ops-service, canonical-ops-repo.postgres.ts and clearSessionForChatJid propagate it; no caller releases yet.

S11 lint gate: a package.json script lint:changed (ESLint over the TypeScript files changed against the merge-base with origin/main) runs inside FACTORY_STRUCTURAL_CMD in .envrc and as the blocking CI check step; full npm run lint stays an advisory continue-on-error CI step; every file this task touches is lint-clean; the 82 pre-existing errors outside the diff are recorded as deferral D-0080 with a trigger and are neither fixed, baselined nor suppressed here.

S10 unchanged behaviour: the four pinned tests (group-processing 'passes hydrated memory context with provider session resume id', agent-runner-ipc 'resumes and persists SDK sessions for live channel turns', claude-agent-sdk-boundary 'passes hermetic Gantry capabilities and settings into the Claude SDK', deepagents-memory-context 'injects the trust-scoped memory block exactly once as a model-visible user message') and the scheduled-job tests are untouched and green; python3 factory/scripts/verify.py is green.

Task-specific seam: the two new repository operations are single SQL statements whose predicates are the whole safety story — the null-safe reset_at fence must appear in BOTH raise and retire, and retire must be the only path that flips active→expired and must RETURN the row it flipped; the compaction-delta degradation path is deliberately left on the old expire helper (ready row) and must not be 'cleaned up' into retire. Inline lanes mirror the same shape in their own modules. resetScope's return is readonly and never undefined. The migration is generated by drizzle-kit and committed as emitted. Deferred to T2 with TODO(T2): reading the mark for policy and raising it after runs — T1 only exposes the operations and the projection; deferred to T3: consuming the retired references.

tasks.title: Ceiling policy, the cap setting, and event types
tasks.objective: Turn T1's measured high-water mark into policy: clamp it at the column's limit so an extreme observation cannot fail the write and leave an over-cap session resumable, add the operator-settable cap to the limits settings pipeline, refuse to resume a session whose mark exceeds that cap and retire it instead, raise the mark after every usage-bearing run, register both retirement event families with payloads discriminated on the reason and publish the three that do not belong to `/new`, collect the retired references for T3 to release, and leave the operator the procedures and the schema-checked observability recipe.
acceptance_criteria: S4 post-run raise: a run that ends in error but reported usage raises the mark through raiseProviderSessionContextHighWaterMark with the model-visible input tokens T1 computes; a run that reported no usage does not call the operation at all (not with zero, not with undefined).

THE OVERFLOW CLAMP: the stored mark is clamped at 2,147,483,647 — the limit of the `integer` column at schema/sessions.ts:89 — in domain/sessions/provider-session-measurement.ts, at the domain boundary and not in SQL. The constant derives from the column type, NOT from the limits parser's 900,000 maximum: a real mark can exceed 900,001 on a ~1M-context model, and coupling the two would let a widened cap range leave a clipped mark unable to exceed the cap, silently ending retirement for exactly the sessions the ceiling targets. Covered at the boundary: 2,147,483,647 stores unchanged, above it clamps, and a negative or non-integer still raises ProviderSessionMeasurementError.

S5 ceiling preflight: an over-cap session is not passed as the resume id; retirement returns the reference; the run proceeds fresh; the replacement handle is persisted; the reply is delivered; a run that CROSSES the cap mid-run is retired on the FOLLOWING resume, never mid-run; a `maintenance_compact` row is not retired; a `ready` row is promoted first (the preflight sits after prepareCompactionDeltaReplay and after the access-fingerprint check, and evaluates the mark on the SELECTED row only); a lost transition persists no replacement.

R6 lost-race re-read, BOTH branches: on a lost ceiling transition the turn context is re-read with `hydrateMemory: false`, and the carried memory block is reused ONLY when the agent session id and the null-normalised `reset_at` generation both still match. On a mismatch the carried block is DISCARDED and memory rehydrated, because decision 0078's exactly-once hydration is per turn and a mismatch means a concurrent reset. Both branches carry regression coverage — a match-only implementation would leak a retired session's memory into the replacement.

S6 no regression for healthy sessions: an under-cap or unmarked session resumes with its memory block and snapshot, and these four pinned tests stay green and UNTOUCHED — apps/core/test/unit/runtime/group-processing.test.ts "passes hydrated memory context with provider session resume id", apps/core/test/unit/runner/agent-runner-ipc.test.ts live-turn persist/resume, apps/core/test/integration/claude-agent-sdk-boundary.integration.test.ts memory+prompt user message, and apps/core/test/unit/adapters/deepagents-memory-context.test.ts.

S7 the cap setting: `limits.provider_session_max_input_tokens` parses beside the existing per-provider entries in runtime-settings-limits-parser.ts (which today accepts only `<providerId>.requests_per_minute`), defaults to 150,000, rejects values outside 20,000-900,000 with a PATH-LEVEL error, round-trips through the revision document and the desired-state export, is applied from a new revision by a current worker, and a worker below the bumped reader version holds its prior revision and alerts. CURRENT_SETTINGS_READER_VERSION goes 15 -> 16 (settings-fleet-import.ts:71). The canonical YAML renderer must emit the block for a scalar-only cap: renderLimitsSettingsYaml (runtime-settings-optional-blocks-renderer.ts:27) returns early when `limits.providers` is empty, so a cap configured without any per-provider entry is silently dropped from settings.yaml and does not survive a round-trip.

S9 event TYPES and the three non-`/new` publications, with R5's envelope: `session.provider.retired` and `session.provider.cleanup_failed` are registered runtime event types. ONLY `session.provider.retired` carries a payload DISCRIMINATED on `reason` in {ceiling, fingerprint, missing, new} — `providerSessionHash` (full lowercase hex SHA-256 of the raw external session id) and `executionProviderId` always, `contextHighWaterMark` and `cap` ONLY for `reason = ceiling`. `session.provider.cleanup_failed` is a SEPARATE, flat payload type `{providerSessionHash, executionProviderId, error}` (spec:215) and is NOT reason-discriminated; conflating the two was a defect in the first draft of this criterion. RuntimeEventPublishInput carries `payload: unknown` (domain/events/events.ts:103) with six or more consumers across app/bootstrap/, so a standalone interface binds nothing: these families publish through a typed helper that narrows the payload, such that a wrong payload for a `reason` FAILS TO COMPILE. T2 publishes all three of ceiling and fingerprint at preflight with `sessionId = agentSessionId` and no run id, and missing-session after the failed attempt with THAT attempt's `runId` — each with its own test, fingerprint included. Publication is best-effort in the sense the spec states and no stronger: a publication FAILURE never suppresses the reply. Proof covers publish, query AND projection for both families. T2 does NOT publish the `/new` event — T3 owns both `/new` handlers.

The retired-reference handover to T3: `GroupAgentRunResult` is the bare union 'success' | 'error' | 'stopped' (group-agent-runner.ts:59) and widening it would edit group-processing-types.ts:81, which T3 owns. So T2 adds an OPTIONAL typed sink to runAgent's options object — a `readonly RetiredProviderSessionReference[]` collector — and each of its three retirement sites (ceiling preflight, access-fingerprint at :394, missing-session at :514) pushes the reference retirement now returns, in retirement order. Absent sink is a no-op that cannot throw. T3 supplies the sink and drains it in group-processing.ts after the complete primary-plus-fallback delivery attempt settles. T2 does not touch group-processing.ts, group-processing-types.ts or group-processing-session-command-handlers.ts.

S12 and R7 operator documentation: docs/memory/provider-session-ceiling-operations.md holds the pre-deploy reset with its stop condition, the orphan scan, and the observability recipe. The recipe SQL is EXTRACTED FROM THE DOCUMENT by the test and executed against the current schema by a Postgres integration test, so the document cannot drift from the schema silently. R7: docs/architecture/canonical-domain-model.md:165 no longer states that fresh runs restore durable Gantry memory only (runtime-components.md was already corrected).
S10 and S11: the scheduled-job tests are untouched and green, and `python3 factory/scripts/verify.py` is green including the diff-scoped `npm run lint:changed`.

The public desired-state payload: the approved plan classes T2's API impact as CHANGED and assigns T2 a control-API round trip — PUT a document carrying `limits.provider_session_max_input_tokens` to `/v1/settings/desired-state`, GET it back, and assert the value survives the public surface. The plan states this is the only proof the field is reachable through the API whose payload shape it changes, so it is T2's and not deferrable to T4; T4 still owns the typed request/response DTO and the OpenAPI registry entry. No route SOURCE change in T2 — the existing untyped route already returns the revised document.

The FIRST mark on a fresh or replacement session: the post-run raise must record a mark for a session created or replaced during this turn, not only for one that was resumed. `setSession` returns `Promise<boolean | void>` (domain/repositories/ops-repo.ts:441) and yields no ids, so the runner raises using the `nextSessionId` it just persisted as BOTH the internal provider-session id and the external session id. That is correct because the Postgres adapter inserts `id: sessionId` AND `externalSessionId: sessionId` (canonical-session-repository.postgres.ts:498,501) — an adapter detail the port never promised, so T2 pins it with a test asserting the invariant, plus a test that a fresh session's first turn records a mark. Ravi's ruling at the T2 task grill (2026-09-11), chosen over a non-hydrating context re-read (more robust but an extra query per fresh session) and over leaving the first mark NULL (which would let one long first turn take an extra oversized resume).

tasks.reviewer_focus: Load-bearing canon: pnp-coding-standards-modular-monolith.md (typed constants over literals, domain error types, policy out of data access) and 0025-settings-authority.md (the cap is settings-owned, read through the revision pipeline, never an env var). Task-specific seams, in the order they are most likely to be got wrong: (1) the clamp constant derives from the `integer` column's limit, NOT from the limits parser's 900,000 maximum — a reviewer who sees 900,001 or any expression over the cap bounds must reject it, because that coupling silently ends retirement when the cap range widens; (2) the clamp is at the domain boundary, not in SQL; (3) the preflight sits after prepareCompactionDeltaReplay and after the fingerprint check and reads the cap ONCE per turn, evaluating the mark on the selected row only; (4) BOTH R6 branches are proven — a match-only re-read leaks a retired session's memory; (5) the event payload discrimination actually fails to compile when a `reason` carries the wrong fields, which RuntimeEventPublishInput's `payload: unknown` does not give for free; (6) publication is best-effort exactly as the spec states — a FAILURE never suppresses the reply; do not demand more than that, the approved criterion makes no latency promise; (7) the retired-reference sink is an optional options field, so T3's files stay untouched and an absent sink cannot throw; (8) the observability SQL is extracted from the operations document rather than duplicated in the test.

tasks.title: The desired-state settings contract
tasks.objective: Give /v1/settings/desired-state a typed request and response DTO and register it in the OpenAPI registry. The route accepts settings?: unknown and returns record-shaped JSON today, and the registry documents /v1/settings but not this path, so the payload that limits.provider_session_max_input_tokens changes is an untyped, undocumented public surface. Separated from T2 because it is a public HTTP contract with its own canon requirements.
acceptance_criteria: API-1: PUT /v1/settings/desired-state accepts a typed request DTO — no `unknown` at the boundary — and rejects a malformed body with a path-level error rather than accepting it and failing later in the parser.

API-2: GET /v1/settings/desired-state returns a typed response DTO whose shape includes limits.provider_session_max_input_tokens, so the field T2 added is part of the declared contract rather than incidental record-shaped JSON.

API-3: the path is registered in the OpenAPI registry with request and response schemas that match the implementation, satisfying the endpoint-documentation standard; a schema that drifts from the handler fails the check.

API-4: a PUT/GET round trip proves the new limits key survives the public surface unchanged, and the settings pipeline T2 built behaves identically — this task changes the contract's typing and documentation, not its behaviour.
